recipes.name: Cucumber Raita
ingredients_raw: 2 hot house cucumber - peeled, seeded and thinly sliced

steps.text: Stir yogurt, cucumber, lemon juice, mint, sugar, and salt together in a bowl. For best results cover and refrigerate the raita for a few hours, or preferably overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Cucumber Raita
raw_recipe.description: Raita is easy to make at home with yogurt, cucumber, and fresh mint for a cool, refreshing, delicious dip, sauce, or side dish for Indian dishes.
raw_recipe.name: Cucumber Raita

review.reviewBody: This is my recipe, and I want to explain to the last poster why I use Greek style yogurt. The cucumbers will weep a tremendous amount of liquid, especially if you let this sit all day or overnight. If you do not use a firmer yogurt to start, you will end up with a watery Raita. Since you used regular yogurt and actually added water, perhaps you either used fewer cucumbers, did not let yours sit in the refrigerator to blend the flavors as long as I did, or perhaps you just like it watery. While I agree that Raita should be saucy, I do not think it should be watery, hence the Greek yogurt.

Good recipe with a few points. To everyone saying it's too watery: you need a good quality GREEK yogurt. Most of the store brands are gonna be too runny. It also helps if you seed then chop or grate the cucumbers and the SALT them with Kosher salt. Kosher salt helps to draw out the excess moisture in the cucumbers. Let stand for a hour or two, then since off the salt and let drain. Lastly, FOLD the mint and cucumbers into the yogurt, DO NOT BLEND THEM. Blending will destroy the Greek yogurt's texture, leaving you with a watery raita.

Served this with brown basmati rice , saag paneer, nan and some other things the other day. It isn't necessary to use only greek yogurt. Just let drain some regular non fat yogurt through a fine seive/coffee filter. I used fresh yogurt I made the day before. This recipe can be used in so many ways. I even use it for salad dressing! Delicious; so refreshing!

very delicious and authentic tasting recipe. I suggest using greek yogurt instead of trying to substitute it with regular plain yogurt to get a creamier and less watery texture. i grated 1 cucumber and strained it very well through a paper towel. i just put the it in the paper towel and squeezed all the liquid out and dumped the shredded cucumber with the sauce and it came out GREAT. i liked having the subtle taste of cucumber instead of chunks of it. =) very delicious!

Regarding "Greek style" yogurt, if you cannot find it and you don't want watery Raita, then you can add a Tbls or so of thick sour cream. This will help bind it. Also, you can chop the cukes in advance, sprinkle with the salt and let sit for an hour. Then drain off the liquid before adding the rest of the ingredients. Lastly, I completely omit the lemon juice and just serve lemon wedges on the side.

Just did not need 24 servings as there are only 2 of us, so made enough to satisfy the salad and peri peri chicken. Sliced cuke as suggested and then salted to draw out water and retain crispness. Added a sugar and smoked salt mix that I had left over from brining the chicken. Worked out well. Thumbs up from me.👍🏻🍏

turned out wonderful for me. Just a quick tip, I used Cabot (like the cheese) brand greek yogurt because it's ridiculously thick (thickest I've seen so far). Turned out awesome, although the cucumber does water it down a bit. Mix in some spices of your liking a little bit at a time ( you can always add more). I did dill and cumin. Gets more flavorful with a few hours/day of sitting. I paired it with a red lentil curry from allrecipes and it was just heavenly.

I prepared this as more of a condiment than a salad, because that's what I was after for my purpose. It's also awesome as a salad!
I used 1 regular, peeled cuke and shredded it with the corse side of a box grater. I put it in a fine sieve and sprinkled it with some kosher salt, stirred it well and sprinkled another pinch of salt on it. I let this drain @ 15-20 minutes while I assembled the other ingredients. This draws out much of the moisture and keeps the cuke from watering down the raita. Otherwise, I followed the recipie as printed, cutting all in half since I only used one cuke. This was a FANTASTIC topping for Yakuta's Indian Style Sheekh Kabab elsewhere on this site. In fact, the two go together so well, I'll not make the kababs without this raita!

This is just what I was looking for. I added one small clove of garlic and it was perfect for what I remember from the Middle East. I used regular yogurt, which I strained, and I did salt the cucumbers and let them drain also. It was not too watery, just right. Thanks for this recipe!
Didn't change anything but the process for the cucumber. Instead of slicing, grate. Press between paper towels to extract about 50% of the liquid. Then add to the yogurt. Lot less runny.

Great basic Raita recipe! 
Tastes great with Jeera (cumin) chicken. Make sure you taste, add mint/cucumbers as needed. If letting refrigerate overnight, you need less cucumber and mint of course! Can adapt with grapes, onions, tomatoes, etc to make it suit your dish. It's nice to add just a dash of a little chili (cayenne) powder and ground cumin.

(The review that said mint didn't make it authentic to Indian food doesn't make much sense. They use a ton of mint over there. There are many types of raita.)

I love the simplicity of this recipe. So many other recipes overcomplicate Raita. Use less lemon as it overwhelmed the flavour, added more mint and cucumber to compensate. l also grated the cucumber. Great idea adding sugar, it really pulled the flavours together
Love this so fresh. Put some cumin in.
Maybe leave out the sugar next time.
Yum ! good thing this is low in calories because I can't stop eating it. I did add chopped chives and dried dill.
Added onion
Will make this again but did think it was a little to much cucumber.
very good . i couldn't find fresh mint in 4 different stores , had to use dried , but it was still delicious .

Very good. I like to have raita whenever I make a curry. I added very finely chopped red bell pepper, and I've never added sugar before, but it makes a nice difference. I used "skyr" yogurt which is REALLY thick, so there was no need to strain the cucumber. I grate the cucumber, including the skin. More fiber and very yummy!
I made it today to go with lamb tagine. The raita came out delicious, so cooling and refreshing. I used a bit more fresh mint than the recipe called for, because I like mint a lot.
